summary: 4 acceptance criteria exercised via 5 artifacts (1 re-run backend suite + 4 browser checks, 1 reused from iteration 3). 2 passed, 2 failed with a real, reproducible frontend bug (same root cause) in AudioRecorder.tsx; 1 flaky note on the reused cleanup check n/a. 0 blocked/test_error.

bugs.criterion: In-test recorder produces playable captured audio
bugs.description: Stopping a non-empty Speaking recording never shows the in-test playback control ('practice-recording-playback') and never sends the captured audio to /api/pte/transcribe. Root cause isolated in frontend/src/components/AudioRecorder.tsx: recorder.onstop starts with `if (!mountedRef.current) return;` (line 59), but `mountedRef` (useRef(true), line 17) is only ever set to `false` in the unmount cleanup effect (lines 26-32) and is NEVER set back to `true`. Under React.StrictMode (enabled in main.tsx), React's dev-mode mount→cleanup→remount dance runs that cleanup once synchronously right after the first mount, permanently flipping mountedRef.current to false for the life of the component instance — even though the component is still actually mounted and working (the elapsed-duration ticker, start/stop buttons, etc. all continue to function normally). Every subsequent recorder.onstop call therefore returns immediately, before the blob-from-chunks construction, the blob.size check, the transcription upload, or any onError call.
bugs.evidence: Instrumented the page (console + network + Array.prototype.push + Blob constructor spies) around a start->wait-for-advancing-duration->stop flow with a MediaRecorder mock that emits a real non-empty chunk via ondataavailable before stop() is called. Confirmed: the chunk IS pushed into the component's chunks array before stop (BLOB PUSH size=16 arrLenBefore=0), recorder.stop() IS invoked and this.onstop() IS called (CALLING onstop for id=2 logged) -- yet no 'new Blob(chunksRef.current,...)' construction ever logs, no request to /api/pte/transcribe ever fires (network listener saw zero requests), and no toast/error appears at any point (screenshots immediately-after-stop and half-second-after-stop show plain idle UI with 'Enable microphone & record' and no playback element). The visible '1s captured' text is leftover from the elapsed ticker during recording, not evidence that onstop's own setElapsed ran. This is consistent with the mountedRef early-return theory and not with any transcription/network failure (ruling out a backend-side cause).

bugs.criterion: Empty capture reports a useful error
bugs.description: Stopping a Speaking recording that captured zero audio chunks does NOT show the expected 'No audio was captured. Check that the correct microphone is selected...' message. Same root cause as above: the mountedRef guard in AudioRecorder.tsx's recorder.onstop (line 59) returns before the `if (!blob.size) { onError(...); return; }` check is ever reached, so the useful capture-failure message is never surfaced to the user; the UI silently reverts to the idle 'Record your response' state with no answer captured and no explanation.
bugs.evidence: Same instrumentation as above with a MediaRecorder mock that never emits ondataavailable (0 chunks). After Stop: page.getByText(/No audio was captured.../i) never becomes visible (10s timeout, element not found); module-answer-state stays 'No answer recorded yet' (correct — nothing was wrongly submitted) but with no error message at all, and the /api/pte/transcribe endpoint was never called (transcribeCalled=false), confirming the code returns before either the error path or the upload path.

action_items.detail: In frontend/src/components/AudioRecorder.tsx, reset mountedRef.current = true at the top of startRecording (or on mount via a mount-effect), or restructure the mount/unmount tracking so React.StrictMode's dev-mode double-invoke of the unmount cleanup does not permanently disable the onstop handler. This currently makes EVERY speaking recording in this build produce no playback, no transcript, and no error message after Stop — a total break of the Speaking practice/test flow's core recording feature in the dev environment used for testing.
